name: Orvar, the All-Form
oracle_text:
Changeling
Whenever you cast an instant or sorcery spell, if it targets one or more other permanents you control, create a token that's a copy of one of those permanents.
When a spell or ability an opponent controls causes you to discard this card, create a token that's a copy of target permanent.
blocked_sentences: Whenever you cast an instant or sorcery spell, if it targets one or more other permanents you control, create a token that's a copy of one of those permanents.
When a spell or ability an opponent controls causes you to discard this card, create a token that's a copy of target permanent.

needs.what: Two halves of one mechanic, both hanging off the `spell_cast` event. (1) An intervening-if a `spell_cast` trigger can ask about the *triggering spell's own targets* -- "if it targets one or more other permanents you control" -- i.e. a condition that resolves the chosen targets of the spell that just went on the stack, filters them by an ordinary selector (permanent, controller `you`, `exclude_self`) and is true when at least one survives. (2) A binding that carries that same filtered set of targeted permanents into the ability's effects, so `copy_permanent` can be pointed at one of them (`objects: {"binding": "spell_targets", "count": 1}` with the controller choosing, per 'one of those permanents'). Concretely: put the spell's target oids on the SPELL_CAST payload in `Game._cast` (src/automtg/engine/game.py:703, which today carries only player/source/oid/spell_oid/sid/card/kicked), add that key to `EVENT_BINDING_KEYS` (src/automtg/engine/triggers.py:1056) so it reaches `event_bindings`, and add a condition key that filters it. Both halves are needed together -- the condition alone would make the card copy an arbitrary permanent, which is a different and much stronger card.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: The `spell_cast` trigger's `filter` reads characteristics of the spell card only (types, colors, mana_value); nothing in `selector_keys`, `condition_keys` or `trigger_keys` reaches another object's targets. `{"target": "t1"}` is the near miss and is the wrong scope by construction: `selectors.py` resolves it through `ctx.target_oids`, which is the *ability's own* declared target specs (the source comment at selectors.py:1060 says exactly this), so it can never name what somebody else's spell chose. `becomes_target` is the other near miss and is a per-permanent trigger: it fires on the permanent being targeted, so writing it on Orvar would only ever see spells aimed at Orvar himself, and there is no way to put a trigger on every permanent you control. The SPELL_CAST event carries no target information at all (game.py:703), so even a new condition key would have nothing to read, and `EVENT_BINDING_KEYS` has no list-of-oids entry for a spell's targets (`attackers` is the only list binding and is combat-only). Approximating it as an unconditional `spell_cast` trigger plus `copy_permanent` over `{"zone": "battlefield", "controller": "you", "exclude_self": true}` would fire on targetless spells and copy any permanent, not one the spell targeted -- strictly stronger, so it was not written.

needs.what: A `discard` trigger able to say *who caused the discard* and to fire from the discarded card's own hand: "When a spell or ability an opponent controls causes you to discard this card". Needs (a) the cause's controller recorded on the DISCARD event -- `discard_cards` / `primitives.py:100` currently fires `EventType.DISCARD` with only `player`, `source` and `oid`, so nothing distinguishes an opponent's Mind Rot from a cleanup-step discard, your own rummaging, or a discard paid as a cost -- exposed as a trigger clause (e.g. `cause_controller: "opponent"` on the trigger, matching the spelling `double_triggers` already uses for statics), and (b) the discard being a spell-or-ability effect rather than a turn-based action or a cost. The ability must function while the card is in hand and match only itself (`active_zones: ["hand"]` plus a `self_only` filter on the discarded card); the effect half, `copy_permanent` at a target permanent, already exists.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `trigger_keys` has `controller`, but on a `discard` trigger `_actor` deliberately returns `event.player` -- the player who *discarded* (triggers.py:1185 and the comment above it) -- so `controller: "opponent"` would mean "an opponent discarded a card", not "an opponent made you discard". `not_cause` compares `event.data["cause"]`, which the discard event never sets. `cause_controller`/`cause_events`/`cause_filter` exist only on the `double_triggers` static (loader/__init__.py:2574, triggers.py:_cause_matches) and are read from a battlefield static, not from a triggered ability, and not for DISCARD. Writing the line as a plain `discard` trigger with `controller: "you"` would fire on every discard you make -- your own cleanup-step discards and any cost you pay with this card -- which is a strictly better card than the printed one, so no partial answer was written. The first line, Changeling, is expressible (an `add_subtype` static over the engine's closed creature-type set) but is not written here because the other two lines are blocked.
